La composizione XRF è stata stimata con: XRF composition was estimated by empirical calibration on standards: net line areas (±1 FWHM window, SNIP background) normalised to the Compton peak, Lucas-Tooth & Price (1961) matrix correction where the number of standards allowed, normalisation to 100% for alloys, uncertainties from leave-one-out cross-validation (cf. Heginbotham et al., 2010, 2015).
Spectra analysed with the XRF 3.0 model:
La composizione XRF è stata calcolata co: XRF composition was calculated by the fundamental-parameters method: primary intensities for a thick homogeneous sample according to Sherman (1955) and secondary fluorescence according to Shiraiwa & Fujino (1966), with cross sections, edge energies and fluorescence yields from xraylib (Schoonjans et al., 2011); the tube spectrum was modelled as a Kramers continuum with anode self-absorption plus characteristic lines (simplified form of Ebel, 1999), with beryllium windows, air path and silicon-detector efficiency. Line areas were obtained by fitting all K, L and M lines of each element (Gaussians with the detector resolution, silicon escape peaks, Rayleigh and Compton scattered tube lines, B-spline background) by weighted non-negative least squares (Lawson & Hanson, 1974), iterating the line ratios predicted for the matrix. Concentrations were normalised to 100% (alloys), as oxides (glass and ceramics), or scaled to the Compton peak with an assumed invisible matrix (paint layers); where stated, the sensitivity of each element was calibrated on standards of known composition. The tube spectrum and fluorescence yields are approximated; without standards the values are semi-quantitative estimates, checked on simulated spectra and not on certified materials.
Spectra analysed with the XRF 3.1 model:
La composizione XRF è stata calcolata co: XRF composition was calculated by the fundamental-parameters method: primary intensities for a thick homogeneous sample according to Sherman (1955), secondary fluorescence according to Shiraiwa & Fujino (1966) and approximate tertiary fluorescence, with cross sections, edge energies, fluorescence yields and Coster–Kronig probabilities from xraylib (Schoonjans et al., 2011); tube spectrum according to Ebel (1999; L lines according to Ebel, 2003), or excitation at declared energies, beryllium windows, air and detector efficiency. Line areas were obtained by fitting all K, L and M lines of each element with the hypermet peak shape (Gaussian with tails and step; Van Gysel et al., 2003), detector Kα and Kβ escape peaks, sum peaks, scattered Rayleigh and Compton tube lines and a B-spline background, as in PyMca (Solé et al., 2007): amplitudes by weighted non-negative least squares (Lawson & Hanson, 1974), energy calibration, resolution and peak shape by Levenberg–Marquardt, iterating the line ratios predicted for the matrix; a proposed element was kept only if its analytical line exceeds 3σ and removing it worsens the fit beyond the threshold. Concentrations were normalised to 100% (alloys), expressed as oxides (glass and ceramics), or referred to the Compton peak with an assumed invisible matrix (paint layers); where stated, the sensitivity of each element was calibrated on standards of known composition. Without standards the values are semi-quantitative estimates.
La massa per area degli strati superfici: The mass per area of surface layers was derived from the ratio of two lines of the same underlying element (Kα/Kβ or Lα/Lβ), R = R₀·exp[−ρd·(μ₁ − μ₂)/sin ψ₂] (Cesareo and Brunetti, 2008; Cesareo et al., 2009; Trojek et al., 2010), or from the attenuation relative to an uncovered area, solving the layered fundamental-parameters model for ρd.
Le quote spettrali delle miscele (minimi: Spectral fractions of mixtures (non-negative least squares on references; Lawson & Hanson, 1974) were converted to weight percentages using relative response factors derived from mixtures of known composition measured under the same conditions.
La taratura multivariata è stata eseguit: Multivariate calibration used PLS1 regression (NIPALS algorithm; Wold et al., 2001) on pre-treated spectra; the number of latent variables was chosen by leave-one-out cross-validation (minimum RMSECV, or the smallest within 5%).
Figure di merito cromatografiche secondo: Chromatographic figures of merit according to USP <621> and Ph. Eur. 2.2.46.
Temperature di onset ed endset estrapola: Extrapolated onset and endset temperatures by the tangent method (ISO 11357-1, ISO 11358-1).
Quantità relativa di spin dal doppio int: Relative spin quantities from the double integral of the derivative spectrum (Eaton et al., 2010).
Integrali relativi riferiti a un segnale: Relative integrals referenced to a signal of known nucleus count (Bharti & Roy, 2012).
Aree nette XRF con incertezza di Poisson: Net XRF areas with Poisson uncertainty and Currie (1968) decision and detection limits.
Rapporto I(D)/I(G) (Tuinstra & Koenig, 1: I(D)/I(G) ratio (Tuinstra & Koenig, 1970) and crystallite size following Cançado et al. (2006).
La struttura secondaria delle proteine è: Protein secondary structure was estimated from the amide I band resolved into Gaussian components located by the second derivative and assigned after Byler & Susi (1986) and Barth (2007).
Resa quantica relativa con il metodo com: Relative quantum yield by the comparative method (Brouwer, 2011).
Chemisorbimento: uptake a impulsi da Σ(A: Chemisorption: pulse uptake from Σ(A_sat − Aᵢ)/A_sat·V_loop, static chemisorption by extrapolation to p = 0 of the combined and repeat isotherms (ASTM D3908), metal dispersion, area and diameter following Bergeret and Gallezot (2008); TPR/TPO/TPD on the measured temperature with a linear baseline, activation energy by Kissinger (1957) and Redhead (1962) with a stated ν; TPR conditions checked with the Monti and Baiker (1983) parameter.
Area specifica BET secondo ISO 9277:2022: BET specific surface area according to ISO 9277:2022, with the range chosen by the Rouquerol et al. (2007) criteria; total pore volume according to Gurvich; mesopore distribution by the BJH method (Barrett et al., 1951) and Dollimore–Heal (1964); isotherm classification according to Thommes et al. (2015).
Le ipotesi qualitative derivano da combi: Qualitative hypotheses derive from combinations of characteristic bands (Socrates, 2001; Larkin, 2011).
Le ipotesi sui materiali derivano dalle: Material hypotheses derive from element combinations (Eastaugh et al., 2008).
